# How much of your winnings actually stays taxable now?

> Free calculator for the OBBBA gambling loss deduction limit: your allowable Schedule A deduction is the lesser of your actual losses or 90% of your winnings, starting with 2026 tax returns. See exactly how much of your winnings becomes taxable "phantom income" even if you broke even or lost overall.

Free and open source (MIT). Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial or professional advice.

## What it answers

Starting with 2026 tax returns, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act caps your gambling-loss deduction at 90% of your winnings — even if you lost just as much as you won. This tool applies that cap to your own numbers and shows the "phantom income" it can create: win $10,000 and lose $10,000, and only $9,000 of the losses is deductible, so $1,000 stays taxable. Only itemizers can deduct losses at all. Source: 26 U.S.C. section 165(d) as amended by Public Law 119-21 (2025), for tax years beginning after 2025. As of 2026-09-25.
